clue.text: Capital hard to find for part of church

parts.note: Paris is the capital city of France
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone hunting a city for a section of a church finds the task difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is the local district served by one church and priest, a subdivision of the wider Church.

clue.text: Awfully nice Duke in concert, in place of royal person

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters and the duke inside the word for the concert

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms in London

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of nice are rearranged

explanation.surface: A duke behaves very pleasantly at a concert, standing in for a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' reads as praise of the duke's niceness but rearranges NICE into INCE. The second 'in' is just a link to the definition, which names a realm, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A princedom is the territory ruled by a prince, so it is the domain of a royal figure.

clue.text: Bring back some brochures to read

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A travel agent tells a customer to return a few leaflets after reading them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' shows the answer runs across brochuRES TO REad.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to return it to its former place or condition, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Chased fame, oddly, being so modest

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters behave strangely, so chased fame is rearranged

explanation.surface: A person who strangely pursued celebrity turned out to be bashful all along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tells you to rearrange CHASED FAME; it does not mean taking odd letters here, since all ten are used. 'being so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shamefaced is bashful and embarrassed, which overlaps with being modest and shy.

clue.text: Icicles collapsed — with 'onset of thaw, that is

indicators.note: icicles that collapse fall into a heap, so the letters of icicles are rearranged
the onset of a word is its beginning, so take its first letter

explanation.surface: Icicles have fallen down as the thaw begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' makes SCILICE from ICICLES; add T from the start of 'thaw'. Scilicet is Latin, abbreviated sc., used in writing to mean 'namely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scilicet is a Latin adverb meaning namely, used to introduce an explanation like the phrase i.e.

clue.text: Dresses impressively to chop down tree

parts.note: to chop is to cut
feeling down means sad
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A lumberjack's instruction to fell a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' reads as a direction for felling but is the adjective meaning unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a dash is an idiom for making a stylish, striking impression, especially through one's clothes.

clue.text: In game of cards, king makes an appearance

parts.note: loo is an old card game
K is the card and chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: During a round of cards, the king finally shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is an old gambling card game, also British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A look is the way something appears to an observer, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Apt to frisk gunman, taking his pieces

parts.note: Samuel Colt was the gun maker behind the Colt revolver

indicators.note: pieces suggests the word his is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A security guard is ready to search a gunman and seize his weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frisk' suggests a body search, but here it means to leap playfully; 'pieces' (guns, in slang) turns HIS into ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Coltish means lively and playful like a young horse, so given to prancing about.

clue.text: Drunk keels over before end of party

parts.note: to keel over is to topple, which is to tip

indicators.note: end of means take the last letter of the word party

explanation.surface: A drunk reveller falls over before the party has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsy means slightly intoxicated, a lighter word for being under the influence.

clue.text: Man's town dwelling, a small tower

definitions.meaning: A town on the Isle of Man
a small fortified tower house of the Scottish borders

explanation.definitionFit: Peel is a west-coast Isle of Man port, and a peel tower is a fortified border house.

clue.text: A type of tray, say, put into office

parts.note: an in-tray holds incoming papers on a desk
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Someone describes a kind of desk tray before installing it in an office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into office' looks like furnishing a room, but it means appointing someone to a post.
explanation.definitionFit: To instate someone is to install them formally in a position of authority.

clue.text: Loose woman has to sing at start of opera

parts.note: to troll is to sing in a carefree way, as in a round
op. is the standard abbreviation, the opening letters of opera or opus

explanation.surface: A singer of dubious morals must perform at the beginning of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' and 'at' are links. Op. abbreviates opus, whose Latin plural is opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollop is a dated insulting term for a sexually promiscuous or slovenly woman.

clue.text: Complex road layout on the next page after 150

indicators.note: after places the word for the next page behind the numeral

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
overleaf means on the other side of the page

explanation.surface: A reader is directed to a road diagram on the page after 150.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloverleaf is a motorway interchange whose looping slip roads resemble a four-leaf clover.

clue.text: Heads off West in large yacht, with lots of craft

indicators.note: heads means the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A sailor sets out westward in a big yacht among plenty of boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests boats, fitting the yachting picture, but means cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Wily means crafty or cunning, full of artful tricks.

clue.text: Sampling of opinion produced by high-speed staff, say

indicators.note: say tells you the words are spoken and give the answer by sound

parts.note: a gallop is a fast run and a pole is a staff

explanation.surface: An opinion survey of rapidly moving employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' reads as employees but is a stick. Gallup is a polling company named after George Gallup.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gallup poll is a survey taken from a sample of people to gauge public opinion.

clue.text: Heard I'd changed? That's unusual for me

definitions.text: Heard I'd changed? That's unusual for me

indicators.note: changed tells you the letters of heard I'd are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A stubborn person responds to rumours of a change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the speaker's reply: such a person would scoff at changing. 'changed' rearranges HEARD I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: A die-hard is a stubborn person who resists change, so changing would be out of character.

clue.text: Find musical entertainment jolly

parts.note: a disco is a dance event with recorded music
in British speech jolly means very, as in jolly good

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a music event is great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' means very in British English ('jolly good').
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is something found, so the noun find is a synonym.

clue.text: Primates outside a church for Indians

indicators.note: outside means the word for the primates wraps around the other letters

parts.note: apes are primates

explanation.surface: Monkeys gather outside a church instead of Native Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primates' could suggest bishops, fitting the church, but here they are animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apaches are Native American peoples of the south-western United States.

clue.text: Instrument provided right time in plant

parts.note: the sax is a musical instrument, short for saxophone
provided means if, as in on condition that
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A musician has an instrument, given the right moment, in a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxifrage is a low-growing rock plant with small star-shaped flowers.

clue.text: Reverse intention. in wholesale folly

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for wholesale

parts.note: mass means on a large scale, as in mass production

indicators.note: reverse tells you the word for intention is read backwards

parts.note: an end is an aim or intention

explanation.surface: A U-turn on a plan amid large-scale stupidity.
explanation.walkthrough: The full stop after 'intention' is misleading punctuation; 'Reverse' looks like a verb commanding the reader but turns the word for intention into DNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness and folly both mean extreme foolishness or senseless behaviour.

clue.text: Mother Goose is absurd

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
a goose is a silly person, a fool

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme character is called ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother Goose' reads as the nursery-rhyme figure but splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Damfool is an informal adjective meaning utterly stupid or ridiculous.

clue.text: Statesman left in Israeli city to vote

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the city name

parts.note: Haifa is a port city in northern Israel
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A politician, abandoned in an Israeli city, goes to the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Halifax was a British Foreign Secretary in the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Halifax was a leading British politician and diplomat of the Second World War era.

clue.text: Place where you'll find keys for a lid, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among several, so the letters of for a lid are reworked

explanation.surface: Keys needed to unlock a lid could be anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keys' suggests locks, but the Florida Keys are a chain of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida Keys are a chain of coral islands off the southern tip of the US state.

clue.text: Unconvincing material

definitions.meaning: a feeble excuse is weak and hard to believe
a shimmering cloth woven with metallic threads

explanation.definitionFit: A weak excuse is described as lame; lamé is a glittering fabric with metal threads.

clue.text: King William almost raised a balance

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the pieces read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: Bill is a short form of William

explanation.surface: A king called William lifted up a pair of scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims BILL to BIL; R + BIL is then reversed by 'raised' to give LIBR.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra is the zodiac constellation pictured as a pair of scales used for weighing.

clue.text: Impervious to disturbance from robust demonstration

parts.note: sound means healthy and robust
a proof is a demonstration that something is true

explanation.surface: Someone untroubled by noise after a strong display.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundproof means preventing noise from passing through, so unaffected by outside noise.

clue.text: Recognises, we hear, some of the voters

indicators.note: we hear signals that the answer is a word spoken that sounds like another

parts.note: to recognise someone is to know them

explanation.surface: Some of the electorate are recognised, we're told.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament, those voting against a motion are called the noes.
explanation.definitionFit: The noes are those who vote against a motion, so part of the voting body.

clue.text: High-spirited

definitions.meaning: high meat has been hung until strong-smelling

explanation.definitionFit: Gamy means smelling strongly like hung game meat, and also plucky or spirited.

clue.text: Cape, in general, finished with English fabric

indicators.note: finished with puts the letter for English at the very end
in places the letter for cape inside the word for general

parts.note: broad means general, as in a broad outline
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A general wearing a cloak ended up with English cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' reads as an officer, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Brocade is a rich fabric woven with raised patterns, often in gold or silver thread.

clue.text: Alien objects to CIA improperly following former partner

indicators.note: following places the rearranged letters after the word for former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: improperly suggests something done wrongly, so the letters of to CIA are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests to the CIA about the behaviour of an ex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'objects' reads as a verb but is a noun in the definition; 'improperly' turns TO CIA into OTICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are curious items from foreign lands, things strange and unfamiliar.

clue.text: It's not just a pupil I have that's rubbish

definitions.text: It's not just a pupil I have
definitions.meaning: playfully, the whole organ belonging to me rather than only the pupil

explanation.definitionFit: All my eye is dated slang for nonsense; read literally it is the entire organ, not just the pupil.

clue.text: Stick split

explanation.definitionFit: Cleave is a contronym: it means both to adhere closely and to split apart.
